claim: 42% of MHS patients have hyperglycemia
source: 42% of MHS patients have hyperglycemia.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a finding from the patient cohort

claim: Phosphorylated glycogen phosphorylase (GPa) is elevated in microsomal extracts from MHS patients' muscle
source: phosphorylated glycogen phosphorylase (GPa), glycogen synthase (GSa) – respectively activated and inactivated by phosphorylation – and their Ca2+-dependent kinase (PhK), are elevated in microsomal extracts from MHS patients' muscle.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by Western blot data in Figure 3

claim: Glycogen synthase (GSa) is elevated in microsomal extracts from MHS patients' muscle
source: phosphorylated glycogen phosphorylase (GPa), glycogen synthase (GSa) – respectively activated and inactivated by phosphorylation – and their Ca2+-dependent kinase (PhK), are elevated in microsomal extracts from MHS patients' muscle.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6

claim: Phosphorylase kinase (PhK) is elevated in microsomal extracts from MHS patients' muscle
source: phosphorylated glycogen phosphorylase (GPa), glycogen synthase (GSa) – respectively activated and inactivated by phosphorylation – and their Ca2+-dependent kinase (PhK), are elevated in microsomal extracts from MHS patients' muscle.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by Western blot data in Figure 6

claim: Glycogen is decreased in MHS patients' muscle
source: Glycogen and glucose transporter GLUT4 are decreased.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by glycogen assay data in Figure 8

claim: GLUT4 is decreased in MHS patients' muscle
source: Glycogen and glucose transporter GLUT4 are decreased.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and supported by Western blot data in Figure 8

claim: Increased cytosolic calcium concentration promotes GP phosphorylation
source: [Ca2+]cytosol, increased to MHS levels, promoted GP phosphorylation.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and demonstrated experimentally in Figure 7

claim: GPa is located at sarcoplasmic reticulum junctional cisternae
source: Imaging at ~100 nm resolution located GPa at sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) junctional cisternae, and apo-GP at Z disk.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and demonstrated by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 5

claim: Apo-GP is located at Z disk
source: Imaging at ~100 nm resolution located GPa at sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) junctional cisternae, and apo-GP at Z disk.
evidence: Stated in the abstract and demonstrated by immunofluorescence imaging in Figure 4

claim: High cytosolic calcium activates PhK in MHS muscle
source: MHS muscle therefore has a wide-ranging alteration in glucose metabolism: high [Ca2+]cytosol activates PhK, which inhibits GS, activates GP and moves it toward the SR, favoring glycogenolysis.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental findings

claim: PhK inhibits GS in MHS muscle
source: MHS muscle therefore has a wide-ranging alteration in glucose metabolism: high [Ca2+]cytosol activates PhK, which inhibits GS, activates GP and moves it toward the SR, favoring glycogenolysis.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental findings

claim: PhK activates GP in MHS muscle
source: MHS muscle therefore has a wide-ranging alteration in glucose metabolism: high [Ca2+]cytosol activates PhK, which inhibits GS, activates GP and moves it toward the SR, favoring glycogenolysis.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental findings

claim: PhK moves GP toward the SR in MHS muscle
source: MHS muscle therefore has a wide-ranging alteration in glucose metabolism: high [Ca2+]cytosol activates PhK, which inhibits GS, activates GP and moves it toward the SR, favoring glycogenolysis.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a conclusion from the experimental findings

claim: The metabolic alterations in MHS patients probably cause hyperglycemia
source: The alterations probably cause these patients' hyperglycemia.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as an inference from the observed metabolic changes

claim: Skeletal muscle is the major processing site for dietary glucose
source: Skeletal muscle is the major processing site for dietary glucose, consuming it at a high rate during exercise and storing it as glycogen more than any other tissue (Baron et al., 1988; Mizgier et al., 2014).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations

claim: Muscle failure to take up glucose heralds the eventual onset of type 2 diabetes
source: Muscle is critical to glucose homeostasis, to the point that its failure to take up glucose heralds the eventual onset of type 2 diabetes (DeFronzo and Tripathy, 2009).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citation

claim: Insulin induces intracellular Ca2+ release sufficient for a modest, transient increase in cytosolic calcium concentration
source: Insulin induces intracellular Ca2+ release sufficient for a modest, transient increase in [Ca2+]cyto (e.g. Contreras-Ferrat et al., 2014; Lanner et al., 2008; Park et al., 2015)
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations

claim: Signaling from contractile activity mediated by increased cytosolic calcium results in increased glucose uptake by insulin-dependent and independent mechanisms
source: reciprocally, signaling from contractile activity mediated by increased [Ca2+]cyto results in increased glucose uptake by insulin-dependent and independent mechanisms (Jessen and Goodyear, 2005; Lanner et al., 2009; Holloszy and Narahara, 1967; Holloszy et al., 1986).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations

claim: Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility is usually linked to mutations in RYR1
source: Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility (MHS) (Litman et al., 2018) is a condition usually linked to mutations in RYR1, which encodes the Ca2+ release channel of the sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR), or in other genes that encode proteins of the skeletal muscle couplon (Stern et al., 1997; Franzini-Armstrong et al., 1999).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations

claim: The primary defect underlying MHS is believed to be a Ca2+ leak from the SR
source: The primary defect underlying this condition is believed to be a 'Ca2+ leak' from the SR, due to an excessive propensity of the RyR channel to open, which in turn leads to increased cytosolic [Ca2+].
evidence: Stated in the introduction as established understanding

claim: Large increases in cytosolic calcium have been found in muscle from MHS individuals
source: Large increases in [Ca2+]cyto have been found in muscle from MHS individuals (López Padrino, 1994; Lopez et al., 1992), MH-susceptible pigs (Lopez et al., 1986) and in myotubes derived from MHS patients (Figueroa et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the introduction with supporting citations

claim: 40.0% of MHS patients had elevated fasting blood sugar
source: As reported (Altamirano et al., 2019), and shown in the box plot (1B), 40.0% (132/329) had elevated fasting blood sugar (FBS, here used as synonymous with 'glycemia'), which is more than double the expected prevalence in the age-matched general population.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1B

claim: There is a positive and highly significant correlation between FBS and FH
source: Additionally, plot 1A shows a positive and highly significant correlation between FBS and FH (r = 0.21, p of no correlation <0.001).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1A showing the correlation

claim: The median FBS was significantly higher in MHS (5.4 mM) than in MHN (5.1 mM)
source: Consistent with the correlation, the median FBS (illustrated in 1B) was significantly higher in MHS (5.4 mM, Inter Quartile Range 4.9–6.9) than in MHN (5.1 mM, IQR 4.8–5.7).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1B

claim: FBS was significantly correlated with age
source: FBS was not significantly different between women and men but it was significantly correlated with age (Panel 1C) and Body Mass Index (BMI, 1D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C

claim: FBS was significantly correlated with Body Mass Index
source: FBS was not significantly different between women and men but it was significantly correlated with age (Panel 1C) and Body Mass Index (BMI, 1D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1D

claim: The MHS condition associates with elevated FBS in an age-independent manner
source: The 1st order regression lines of FH and age are nearly parallel for MHN and MHS, separated by ~0.5 mM, which indicates that the MHS condition associates with elevated FBS in an age-independent manner.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1C

claim: The prevalence of hyperglycemia increases with age
source: The graphs show that the prevalence of hyperglycemia increases with age and is higher in MHS than in MHN at any age.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1E and 1F

claim: The prevalence of hyperglycemia is higher in MHS than in MHN at any age
source: The graphs show that the prevalence of hyperglycemia increases with age and is higher in MHS than in MHN at any age.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 1E and 1F

claim: 22% of the legacy cohort patients are diabetic according to FBS ≥7.0 mmol/L criterion
source: According to criterion #1 (FBS ≥7.0 mmol/L), 22% of the patients in the 'legacy' cohort are diabetic, which more than doubles the prevalence in the general age-matched Canadian population.
evidence: Stated in the Results section based on Diabetes Canada Clinical Practice Guidelines

claim: The content of GP was greater by 119% in the MHS group compared to MHN
source: The content of GP derived from this blot, equal to the sum of GPa and GPb contents, was greater by 119% in the MHS group (p < 0.001; panel 2F and Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2 and Table 1

claim: The 100 kDa band contains glycogen phosphorylase (GP) in high abundance
source: Studied by mass spectrometry (Appendix 1), the 100 kDa and 180 kDa bands contain respectively and in high abundance glycogen phosphorylase (GP) and glycogen debranching enzyme (GDE).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to mass spectrometry analysis

claim: The 180 kDa band contains glycogen debranching enzyme (GDE) in high abundance
source: Studied by mass spectrometry (Appendix 1), the 100 kDa and 180 kDa bands contain respectively and in high abundance glycogen phosphorylase (GP) and glycogen debranching enzyme (GDE).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to mass spectrometry analysis

claim: GDE content was increased by 94% in MHS patients
source: The GDE blot (2C) derived from the gel in 2B confirms the impression, showing a mean content increased by 94% (p = 0.002).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2C

claim: Patients that had higher GP had a commensurate elevation in GDE
source: Patients that had higher GP had a commensurate elevation in GDE (r = 0.94, panel 2H).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 2H showing correlation

claim: The expression levels are altered more for two glycogen breakdown enzymes than any of the major calcium management proteins studied
source: Remarkably therefore, in these subjects bearing a primary calcium handling defect, the expression levels are altered more for two glycogen breakdown enzymes than any of the major calcium management proteins studied here.
evidence: Stated in the Results section as a conclusion from the comparison of protein changes

claim: GP is phosphorylated by phosphorylase kinase (PhK)
source: GP is phosphorylated by phosphorylase kinase (PhK) (Newgard et al., 2000).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation

claim: Phosphorylation at Ser14 converts GP from the apo or b form into GPa
source: Phosphorylation at Ser14 converts GP from the apo or b form into GPa, which promotes the active conformation of the enzyme (Nagy, 2017).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation

claim: PhK is activated by Ca2+
source: Given that PhK is activated by Ca2+ (Brushia and Walsh, 1999) and assuming that MHS patients' [Ca2+]cyto is elevated (see Introduction), we hypothesize that the excess [Ca2+]cyto, via promotion of PhK, leads to an increase in GPa.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with supporting citation

claim: In the whole tissue, GPa was 68% higher in the MHS compared to MHN
source: In the whole tissue, GP was greater in the MHS by 29% (p=0.07), GPa by 68% (p = 4 10-4, Figure 3A,B) and the ratio GPa/GP by 42% (p = 0.005, Figure 3D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3

claim: The ratio GPa/GP in whole tissue was 42% higher in MHS compared to MHN
source: In the whole tissue, GP was greater in the MHS by 29% (p=0.07), GPa by 68% (p = 4 10-4, Figure 3A,B) and the ratio GPa/GP by 42% (p = 0.005, Figure 3D).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3D

claim: In the microsomal fraction GPa content was 70% higher in the MHS
source: In the microsomal fraction GPa content was 70% higher in the MHS (p = 0.05)
evidence: Stated in the Results section

claim: Patients who have high phosphorylation of GP in the whole muscle generally have high GP content in microsomes
source: As shown in Figure 3E, the two variables are positively correlated regardless of MH status (r = 0.72, p = 0.01, Table 2) — patients who have high phosphorylation of GP in the whole muscle generally have high GP content in microsomes.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 3E

claim: GP in its two forms was imaged in muscles at unprecedented resolution
source: GP in its two forms was imaged in muscles of known content of all-forms GP and GPa.
evidence: Stated in the Results section describing the imaging experiments

claim: GP is sometimes present at highest density near the Z disk where it colocalizes with actinin-1
source: As shown in Figure 4, GP (panel Aa) was sometimes present at highest density near the Z disk, where it colocalized with actinin-1 (Ab)
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4A

claim: GP most commonly occupies a slightly wider region in the interior of the sarcomeric I band
source: but in most cases (panels 4 B) it occupied a slightly wider region, always in the interior of the sarcomeric I band, where most mitochondria are located (Bb, see inset for structural guidance).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4B

claim: GP and mitochondrial marker formed I-band patches that remained largely separate
source: As is visually apparent and was confirmed by quantifying colocalization, GP and the mitochondrial marker formed I-band patches that remained largely separate.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4B

claim: Western blots failed to find GP in mitochondrial fractions derived from human biopsies
source: Confirming the separation, Western blots failed to find GP in mitochondrial fractions derived from human biopsies (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: The GP detected in abundance in the microsomal fraction is mostly, if not entirely, the active (GPa) form
source: The putative images of GPb indicate that the GP detected in abundance in the microsomal fraction is mostly, if not entirely, the active (GPa) form.
evidence: Stated in the Results section as a conclusion from imaging analysis

claim: GPa is located close to Casq1, but without actual colocalization
source: The overlays Ac and Bc and the inset in Ac show that GPa is located close to Casq1, but without actual colocalization.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5A and 5B

claim: The images are the first to resolve TC with conventional optics
source: These images are the first to resolve TC with conventional optics (a resolution of ~100 nm is estimated with Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5

claim: STIM1 forms clusters in close proximity to the GPa bands, without actual colocalization
source: STIM1, an integral protein of the SR membrane, appears largely in the sarcomeric I band of mouse muscle (Boncompagni et al., 2017). In panels C and D, GPa delineates clearly the two TC in every triad and STIM1 forms small clusters. GPa and STIM1 can also be found outside triads, at less density, in locations consistent with the longitudinal SR (e.g., 5Dc). Again, there is close proximity but no actual colocalization between these proteins.
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5C and 5D

claim: The average distance between nearest centers of signal mass of GPa and STIM1 is 57 nm
source: A quantitative analysis of colocalization (illustrated with Figure 5—figure supplement 1) yields the average distance between nearest centers of signal mass in objectively located discrete GPa and STIM1 areas (van Steensel et al., 1996). The distance, 57 nm, is consistent with close juxtaposition of molecules within the diameter of a TC in the axial direction of the myofiber (Franzini-Armstrong, 2018 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 5—figure supplement 1

claim: The mean signal of PhK in microsomes was almost 100% higher in the MHS
source: The distribution of the 2-band average is plotted in panel 6E. The mean signal in microsomes was almost 100% higher in the MHS (p = 4 10−4).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6E

claim: In the whole muscle fraction, PhK increased slightly and not significantly
source: In the whole muscle fraction, by contrast, the mean signal increased slightly and not significantly (Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Table 1

claim: The median ratio GSa/GS for band one was higher by 80% in MHS patients but the difference was not significant
source: The median ratio GSa/GS for band one was higher by 80% in MHS patients (Figure 6G) but the difference was not significant (p = 0.11, Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6G and Table 1

claim: GSa/GS was significantly positively correlated with the PhK content in microsomes
source: Although the increase of GSa/GS in MHS cells was not significant by conventional criteria, it was significantly positively correlated with the PhK content in microsomes, as well as with the level of phosphorylation of GP in whole muscle (Panels 5K, L, and Table 2).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 6 and Table 2

claim: Phosphorylation increased at 500 nM calcium concentration
source: As many extracts as applied Ca2+ concentrations were produced for every patient and were aliquoted for quantitative blotting of GP and GPa in separate gels. Blots and gels are shown in Figure 7. The ratio of signals for GPa and GP evolved upon change in [Ca2+] as plotted in Figure 7C, always increasing at the higher [Ca2+] (p < 0.001 in a t test of paired differences).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 7

claim: The median glycogen content was reduced in the microsomes of MHS patients by 43%
source: The results, presented in Figure 8D and Table 1, were expected from the enzymatic changes: the median glycogen content was reduced in the microsomes of MHS patients by 43% (p = 0.01).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8D and Table 1

claim: Glycogen was negatively correlated with PhK and GPa contents of the microsomal and whole muscle fractions
source: Glycogen was negatively correlated with PhK and GPa contents of the microsomal and whole muscle fractions, as illustrated for whole muscle GPa in Figure 8B (r = -0.47, p = 0.02).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8B and Table 2

claim: The content of GLUT4 was lower in the MHS by more than 60%
source: A comparison of the GLUT4 content of the microsomal fraction in MHN and MHS patients is documented in Figure 8C–E. The content was lower in the MHS by more than 60% (p = 0.01, Table 1).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8 and Table 1

claim: There were negative correlations between GLUT4 and PhK and GPa contents of the microsomal and whole muscle fractions
source: There were negative correlations between GLUT4 and PhK and GPa contents of the microsomal and whole muscle fractions, illustrated for whole muscle GPa in Figure 8E (r = -0.46, p = 0.02).
evidence: Stated in the Results section with reference to Figure 8E and Table 2

claim: Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility entails a wide-ranging, pathogenic change in glucose metabolism
source: Our study reveals that Malignant Hyperthermia Susceptibility entails a wide-ranging, pathogenic change in glucose metabolism.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a main conclusion

claim: The changes in glucose processing enzymes result from the primary defect in Ca2+ management that underlies the MHS condition
source: Multiple features of these changes indicate that they result from the primary defect in Ca2+ management that underlies the MHS condition.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data

claim: All MHS patients have a primary defect originated in the couplon
source: Other MHS patients do not have a known diagnostic mutation, but the commonality in clinical features and cellular alterations in MHS animal models (Lopez et al., 1986; MacLennan and Zvaritch, 2011) and human cells (Figueroa et al., 2019) indicates that all have a primary defect originated in the couplon (Stern et al., 1997; Franzini-Armstrong et al., 1999), generally causing excessive release of Ca2+ from the SR.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with supporting citations

claim: Excessive release of Ca2+ from the SR results in partial depletion of SR calcium
source: The consequence is partial depletion of SR calcium, which activates compensatory calcium entry into the cell (SOCE; Michelucci et al., 2018) resulting in elevation of [Ca2+]cyto.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with supporting citation

claim: The changes in PhK content cause the increases in phosphorylation of GP and GS and the decrease in glycogen content
source: Patients who had a marked increase in PhK were found to have substantial changes in the other variables as well. This convergence, quantified by high correlation coefficients between variables (Table 2), indicates that the changes in PhK content cause the increases in phosphorylation of GP and GS and the decrease in glycogen content.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from correlation analysis

claim: The changes in MHS muscle share many features with the program activated during exercise
source: In sum, the results demonstrate in MHS individuals an activation of the pathway of glycogen breakdown to glucose, which shares many features with the program activated during exercise, including a dependence on [Ca2+]cyto, parallel phosphorylation of GP and GS, and decrease in glycogen (rev. Mul et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with supporting citation

claim: The changes in MHS muscle differ from exercise by including an increase in GDE and a decrease in GLUT4 in microsomes
source: However, the changes in MHS muscle differ by including an increase in GDE and a decrease in GLUT4 in microsomes.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a distinction from exercise-induced changes

claim: The chronic increase in cytosolic calcium that occurs in MHS could justify both the increased phosphorylation of PhK, GP and GS and the reduced content of GLUT4
source: In conclusion, the chronic increase in [Ca2+]cyto that occurs in MHS could justify, via distinct but entangled mechanisms, both the increased phosphorylation of PhK, GP and GS and the reduced content of GLUT4 observed in these patients.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the analysis

claim: The reduction in glycogen content would be caused by both the imbalance in the pathway to and from glucose, and a reduction in uptake and availability of glucose
source: In this view, the reduction in glycogen content would be caused by both the imbalance in the pathway to and from glucose, and a reduction in uptake and availability of glucose.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the findings

claim: The metabolic alteration in muscle metabolism is associated with hyperglycemia
source: The metabolic alteration in muscle metabolism is associated with hyperglycemia. This is demonstrated by the relationship between FBS and measures of phosphorylation in the present study.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data

claim: A positive correlation exists between FBS and the ratio GPa/GP of whole tissue (r = 0.58)
source: As shown in Figure 10, a positive correlation exists between FBS and the ratio GPa/GP of whole tissue (r = 0.58), which implies that the metabolic alteration detected among the MHS has systemic consequences that favor high FBS.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with reference to Figure 10

claim: A major part of the excess FBS (0.38/0.5 mM) is related to and potentially explained by the measured changes in glycogen processing enzymes
source: Extrapolation of the present study to the 'legacy' cohort suggests that a major part of the excess FBS (0.38/0.5 mM) is related to and potentially explained by the measured changes in glycogen processing enzymes.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a quantitative analysis of the contribution

claim: The present results identify MHS as a prodrome and cause of hyperglycemia
source: Jointly with the observations of Altamirano et al., 2019, the present results identify MHS as a prodrome and cause of hyperglycemia.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a main conclusion

claim: The alterations justify the increase of the incidence of type 2 diabetes observed in the MHS sample group (22%) over that in the age-matched Canadian population (10%)
source: The alterations justify the increase of the incidence of type 2 diabetes observed in the MHS sample group (22%) over that in the age-matched Canadian population (10%).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a conclusion from the data

claim: The MHS condition imposes changes without changing essential properties
source: The MHS condition — presumably through its higher [Ca2+]cyto — appears to impose changes, such as forcing more of the glycogenolytic enzymes towards the SR, without changing essential properties.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the graded changes observed

claim: The content of GP in microsomes is strictly correlated with its degree of phosphorylation in the whole tissue extract, but not with that in microsomes
source: We now find that the content of GP in microsomes is strictly correlated with its degree of phosphorylation in the whole tissue extract, but not with that in microsomes.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a finding from the biochemical data

claim: All GP in microsomes is in the GPa form
source: This is possible if all GP in microsomes is in the GPa form.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an inference from the correlation data

claim: The present evidence contradicts previous reports that found mostly GPb in a rabbit SR fraction
source: The present evidence contradicts previous reports that found mostly GPb in a rabbit SR fraction, the phosphorylation of which caused its detachment from the SR (Cuenda et al., 1994; Cuenda et al., 1995).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with citations to contradicted studies

claim: The present images suggest a detailed and extensive binding of GPa to the SR
source: The present images suggest instead a detailed and extensive binding of GPa to the SR, perhaps mediated by glycogen as proposed in early studies of GP that distinguished direct and granule-mediated association (Wanson and Drochmans, 1972; Hirata et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an interpretation of the imaging data

claim: GDE has means to associate with the SR other than via glycogen granules
source: The changes in MHS include enrichment of GDE in the microsomal fraction. GDE, however, diminishes together with glycogen in microsomes of exercised rats (Lees et al., 2004). Again, the observations can be reconciled assuming that GDE has means to associate with the SR other than via glycogen granules.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an inference from the observations

claim: GSa and GSb coexist in the membrane system and their relative amounts are regulated in response to changes in calcium
source: While PhK promotes phosphorylation of GP and GS (Brushia and Walsh, 1999; Walsh et al., 1979), the changes in GS observed here differ from those of GP: GSa/GS increases in the microsomal fraction while its total content does not (Table 1). The observations imply that GSa and GSb coexist in the membrane system and their relative amounts are regulated in response to changes in [Ca2+].
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an inference from the data

claim: PhK increases in the microsomes but remains constant in the whole tissue extract
source: As already noted, PhK increases in the microsomes but remains constant in the whole tissue extract. The change thus appears to be a migration of the kinase towards the membrane fraction.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an observation from the data

claim: The six patients identified as metabolically challenged had a disease phenotype greater than average for the MHS class
source: Follow-up of the six patients identified here as metabolically challenged encountered a disease phenotype, quantified by the Clinical Index defined in Figueroa et al., 2019, greater than average for the MHS class.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with reference to a citation

claim: The alterations in glycogen metabolism cause additional health impairment
source: The observation suggests that the alterations in glycogen metabolism cause additional health impairment.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an inference from the follow-up observation

claim: GP Inhibitors decrease FBS
source: GP Inhibitors decrease FBS (Nagy, 2017; Docsa et al., 2011; Pałasz et al., 2019) and increase insulin sensitivity (Docsa et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with supporting citations

claim: GP Inhibitors increase insulin sensitivity
source: GP Inhibitors decrease FBS (Nagy, 2017; Docsa et al., 2011; Pałasz et al., 2019) and increase insulin sensitivity (Docsa et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated in the Discussion with supporting citations

claim: Treating the causes of abnormal Ca2+ handling in MHS should moderate the changes in glycogen metabolism
source: Conversely, treating the causes of abnormal Ca2+ handling in MHS should moderate the changes in glycogen metabolism, as already reported by Altamirano et al., 2019 in their study of an MHS animal model.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as a prediction with supporting citation

claim: The increase of GPa and other proteins precedes hyperglycemia
source: In animal models, the presence of GP in extracellular circulating vesicles is an early marker of cardiac injury (Yarana et al., 2018); in MHS, the increase of GPa and other proteins precedes hyperglycemia, therefore the potential of circulating glucose metabolism enzymes as its early markers should be evaluated.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion as an observation with implications

claim: 560 patients were subjected to the CHCT and studied clinically in the MHIU from 1994 to 2013
source: 560 patients (named the 'legacy' cohort) were subjected to the CHCT and studied clinically in our Malignant Hyperthermia Investigation Unit (MHIU) from 1994 to 2013
evidence: Stated in the Results section describing the patient cohort

claim: 329 patients were diagnosed as MHS and 231 as MHN in the legacy cohort
source: 329 of them were diagnosed as MHS (FH >0.6 g and/or FC >0.2 g) and 231 as MHN.
evidence: Stated in the Results section describing the patient cohort
